p: The new library was designed to be ______: its large windows let in natural light, and its open layout makes it easy for visitors to find their way around.
x: The details after the colon (light, easy to navigate) describe a welcoming space.
t: Nothing about the building suggests it is fragile or temporary.

p: Although the scientist’s early experiments produced ______ results, she refined her methods, and her later trials yielded consistent, reliable data.
x: “Although” sets up a contrast with “consistent, reliable,” so the early results were inconsistent: erratic.
t: “Predictable” means about the same as consistent, so it kills the contrast.

p: Critics praised the novelist’s ______ prose, noting that she could describe a complex scene in just a few carefully chosen words.
x: Describing a lot with few words is economical writing.
t: “Extravagant” is the opposite: wordy and showy.

p: The committee’s report was notably ______: rather than recommending a single course of action, it laid out the benefits and drawbacks of several options and left the final decision to the city council.
x: Presenting both sides of several options without pushing one is evenhanded (fair and balanced).
t: “Partisan” means taking one side, the opposite of what the report did.

p: Many early inventors worked alone, but the Wright brothers ______ closely, dividing tasks and testing each other’s ideas as they developed their flying machine.
x: “But” contrasts with working alone, and “dividing tasks and testing each other’s ideas” is collaboration.
t: Testing each other’s ideas could sound like competing, but dividing tasks shows teamwork.

p: The historian cautioned that the diary, though vivid, should not be treated as a ______ account of the battle, since its author was writing from memory decades later.
x: Writing from memory decades later makes the account less reliable, so it shouldn’t be treated as definitive (final and authoritative).
t: The concern is reliability, not that the diary is made up, so “fictional” misses the point.

p: The hikers were ______ by the storm, so they waited inside the cabin until the rain stopped.
x: Waiting until the rain stopped means the storm delayed them.
t: “Hurried” would mean they moved faster, not that they waited.

p: Some scientists were initially ______ of the new theory, but as more evidence accumulated in its favor, many of them came to accept it.
x: They came to accept it only after more evidence, so at first they doubted it.
t: “Unaware” doesn’t fit: the evidence changed their minds, which means they already knew the theory and doubted it.

p: The artist’s later paintings are more ______ than her early work: where the early canvases depict recognizable landscapes, the later ones consist of shapes and colors with no obvious real-world subject.
x: Shapes and colors with no real-world subject is the definition of abstract art.
t: “Colorful” grabs a word from the text, but the contrast is recognizable versus not recognizable.

p: Because the bridge was built to ______ strong earthquakes, it suffered only minor damage when a major quake struck the region.
x: Minor damage in a major quake means it was built to withstand (resist) earthquakes.
t: A bridge can’t predict or measure quakes, and it certainly shouldn’t cause them.

p: The mayor’s speech was deliberately ______; she avoided committing to any specific policy so that she could adjust her position after hearing from residents.
x: Avoiding any specific commitment on purpose means the speech was deliberately vague.
t: “Concise” means short and clear, and a speech can be short but still specific.

p: The documentary ______ the history of the city’s jazz clubs, tracing their rise in the 1920s, their decline in the 1960s, and their recent revival.
x: Tracing events in order over time is chronicling.
t: A documentary tracing real history doesn’t invent it.

p: Although the chemical is ______ in small amounts, it can become harmful when it builds up in the body over time.
x: “Although” contrasts with “harmful,” so in small amounts it is harmless: benign.
t: “Toxic” means harmful, which destroys the contrast.

p: The coach asked the players to ______ their water bottles before practice so they would stay hydrated in the heat.
x: Staying hydrated requires water, so they should refill their bottles.
t: None of the other actions helps them drink more water.

p: The poet’s use of everyday language made her work ______ to readers who might otherwise have found poetry intimidating.
x: Everyday language helps readers who find poetry intimidating, so it makes the work accessible (easy to approach).
t: “Obscure” means hard to understand, the opposite of the effect described.

p: Rather than ______ the earlier study’s findings, the new research builds on them, using a larger sample to test whether the original results hold in other regions.
x: “Rather than” needs the opposite of building on the findings. Refuting (proving wrong) is that opposite.
t: The new research does extend and partly replicate the study, so saying “rather than” either one contradicts the sentence.
